rules.rationale: Source ESOL: long SMILES strongly reduced solubility (-11.46); anti-correlation implies higher lipophilicity.
Source prior: short SMILES raised solubility (+6.89); small polar molecules should score low on lipophilicity.
Ring role had highest transfer weight (0.758); fused ring systems reduce solubility and add hydrophobic surface.
Donor-count role mapped to hetero bin; polar heteroatoms hydrate readily and depress partition coefficients.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL solubility effects with reversed sign, assuming lipophilicity is anti-correlated with aqueous solubility. Fails if lipophilicity here is driven by polarity balance rather than size, or if the hbond-donor to hetero mapping is invalid.

rules.rationale: Halogen substitution raises hydrophobic surface area and pi-density, a direct mechanistic driver of octanol partitioning.
Extended aromatic systems are nonpolar and poorly hydrated, raising measured logD independent of molecular length.
High heteroatom fraction implies polar and ionizable groups that partition into the aqueous phase.
Counter to low-confidence length transfer: very long strings often encode polar, peptide-like scaffolds, not more lipophilic ones.

skills.hypothesis: Domain-first partition model: halogenation and aromatic surface raise lipophilicity, heteroatom polarity lowers it, and the uncertain length transfer is reversed at the extreme tail. Fails if size dominates polarity in this pool.

fixed_initial.lesson: Cross-endpoint transfer from solubility needs an unverified sign flip, while halogen, aromatic, and heteroatom descriptors map directly onto partition mechanism with broader pool coverage.
fixed_initial.revision_summary: Kept a sign-reversed source-evidence skill using the strongest ESOL roles (length, rings) at reduced confidence, and added a domain-mechanistic counter-hypothesis that downweights the low-confidence length relation (confidence 0.22) in favor of halogenation and aromaticity; the latter is deployed.

rules.rationale: Halogen substitution adds polarizable hydrophobic volume that favors the octanol phase over water.
Extended aromatic frameworks are poorly hydrated and raise logD independently of chain length.
Halogenated aromatics combine pi-density with lipophilic surface, an additive partition gain.
High heteroatom content means polar and ionizable groups that partition into the aqueous phase.

skills.hypothesis: Lipophilicity in this pool is set by a hydrophobic-surface versus polar-heteroatom balance; halogenation and aromaticity raise the score while heteroatom polarity lowers it. Fails if chain length or size dominates polarity here.

rules.rationale: Ring role carried the highest transfer weight (0.758); ring density adds hydrophobic surface and displaces water.
Aromatic ring-rich scaffolds are the concrete carrier of the ring-density effect in this catalog.
Heteroatom-rich rings are polar and hydrogen-bonding, damping the hydrophobic ring gain.
Acyclic or sparse-ring scaffolds expose flexible polar chains to solvent, lowering partition into octanol.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the source ring effect directly, treating ring density as the dominant lipophilic surface proxy rather than reversing any source sign; it deliberately avoids the low-confidence length relation. Fails if ring count is confounded with heteroatom content in this pool.

true_feedback.lesson: Two generations of development seeds agree that the halogen/aromatic surface model with a heteroatom polarity penalty is the reliable signal, while source-derived length transfer stays low-confidence and should be carried only as a structural hedge rather than as a sign-flipped prior.
true_feedback.revision_summary: Deployed the domain-mechanistic halogen/aromatic model again, keeping the halogen-aromatic interaction and the heteroatom penalty with a slightly trimmed penalty weight (0.45) and raised confidence (0.72) after it again led the alternative on development seeds (90.05 vs 88.53 AUC). Replaced the failed sign-flip skill with a ring-density hedge that uses the highest-transfer-weight ring role without inverting any source effect, and dropped the unverified length rules entirely.

rules.rationale: Source ESOL long SMILES cut solubility (-11.46); if solubility and partition anti-correlate, long lipophilic chains favor octanol.
Source prior: short SMILES raised solubility (+6.89); compact polar molecules hydrate well and partition poorly.
Ring role carried the strongest transfer weight (0.758); fused carbocycles add hydrophobic surface that penalizes aqueous solubility.
Donor-count role transferred to heteroatom bin (weight 0.509); polar heteroatoms raise hydration and depress logD.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL size, ring and donor effects with reversed sign under the solubility-partition antipode. Fails if lipophilicity is driven by polarity balance rather than molecular size.

rules.rationale: Moderate halogen load adds polarizable, poorly hydrated surface without excessive molecular weight; raises octanol affinity.
Low heteroatom count means carbon-rich scaffolds with minimal hydration shell, the direct driver of high partition coefficients.
Halogen-free molecules often carry polar functionality instead; absence of lipophilic halogen surface weakens octanol partitioning.
Non-aromatic scaffolds lack extended nonpolar pi surface and often bear hydrophilic groups, lowering the partition score.

skills.hypothesis: Mechanistic partition model: halogen polarizability and hydrocarbon-rich composition raise lipophilicity, while halogen-free and non-aromatic scaffolds partition poorly. Fails if size or ionization dominates composition in this pool.

no_feedback.lesson: Solubility-based transfer needs an unverified sign flip and rests on low-confidence length evidence, so composition descriptors that map directly onto octanol-water partitioning should carry deployment.
no_feedback.revision_summary: Rewrote both skills with single field-value condition maps and at most four rules. Kept the antipode skill but lowered confidence to 0.42 and trimmed its weight on the weak length relation; broadened the domain skill by replacing the narrow halogen_high (98 candidates) rule with halogen_mid gain and halogen_none penalty plus an aromatic_none hydrophilicity rule, and deployed the domain skill.

rules.rationale: ESOL: long SMILES cut solubility (-11.46); anti-correlated endpoint implies greater octanol partitioning.
Source prior: short SMILES raised solubility (+6.89); small polar molecules partition poorly into octanol.
Ring role had the highest transfer weight (0.758); fused rings add rigid hydrophobic surface area.
Donor-to-heteroatom mapping is the weakest source role (0.159), so keep only a mild polarity penalty.

skills.hypothesis: Sign-reversed ESOL transfer: size and ring content raise lipophilicity, small molecules lower it, with a softened heteroatom penalty. Fails if polarity balance rather than molecular size governs partitioning here.

rules.rationale: Polycyclic aromatic cores are poorly hydrated and dominate octanol affinity in drug-like pools.
Rotatable-bond role transferred strongly (0.758); branched alkyl substituents add nonpolar surface area.
Larger scaffolds carry more hydrophobic surface; retained at reduced weight given low length-role confidence (0.224).
Counter to weakest source mapping: moderate heteroatom counts include lipophilic S, N-aryl and halogen contexts.

skills.hypothesis: Counter-hypothesis that removes and mildly reverses the donor-to-heteroatom penalty and leads with an aromatic fused-core interaction. Fails if polar heteroatom content truly suppresses lipophilicity across this pool.

shuffled_feedback.lesson: Across both development generations the sign-flipped ESOL transfer led (88.7 then 90.08 mean AUC) but the ring/branch counter closed to within 0.4 AUC, so the heteroatom penalty is likely weak, not strongly negative; very narrow rules remain the main variance source.
shuffled_feedback.revision_summary: Retained the deployed source-evidence skill with the heteroatom penalty softened further (-0.25 to -0.18) and slightly reduced semantic mass, reflecting the near-tie with the near-zero-penalty counter. Rebuilt the counter as an aromatic fused-core interaction skill that mildly reverses the weakest source mapping (donor to heteroatom, confidence 0.159) while avoiding low-coverage bins such as halogen_high and hetero_none. Deployed the retained transfer skill; sixteen development seeds are too few for causal claims.
